analyst_view.overall: Atalanta arrive in a real slump: a 3-0 home defeat to Parma, then only a draw with Kairat Almaty in the Conference League on Thursday, and Italian papers say Maurizio Sarri's job depends on these games. Sarri is also missing a lot of defenders (Hien, Kossounou, Bellanova, Kristensen) plus Raspadori. Ivan Juric's Monza are without captain Pessina and Folorunsho, and Varela leads the attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Atalanta's attack has stalled: they failed to score at home to Parma and needed Krstovic to rescue a point against Kairat. A coach under pressure usually plays it safer, so we expect a little less than the model, even though both defences are patched up.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Juric's Monza press man-to-man and Sarri's Atalanta like long spells of possession, which roughly balance each other. Nothing in the news moves us away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. Juric's teams play an aggressive man-marking game, and an Atalanta side that is fighting for its coach's job and short of first-choice defenders is likely to be stretched into fouls. That points to a slightly scrappier game than the model has.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots. Both sides want the ball high up the pitch, but Atalanta are low on confidence. We see no clear reason to move far from the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, which is high. Atalanta's attack has been blunt in recent games, and Monza's forward line behind Varela is still being decided (Robinson, Mota, Zeballos and Cutrone are all options), so we expect slightly fewer efforts on target.
